post.summary: Abandon an Organization whose Owner has no account
post.description: Called only by the auth service, when the account write fails after core created the Organization and from its sweep of abandoned sign-ups. Defined by its end state: it answers status deleted whenever no live Organization with this id exists when the call returns (abandoned by this call, deleted or abandoned earlier, or never created), so success does not mean this call deleted it and a repeat, with the same key, a new key or another user, answers success. A live Organization is abandoned only if it is active (a suspended one is never abandoned: a suspension is deliberate), has exactly one member, that member is the userId and it was created less than 24 hours ago by the database clock; otherwise organization.not_abandonable and nothing changes. The check and the delete are one transaction holding the Organization lock, so a concurrent accept either lands first (then this refuses) or finds the Organization deleted. The only member is removed in the same transaction, so the user id is free when it returns; Teams, Invitations and the rest are left to the deletion job, and a pending Invitation can no longer be accepted.

post.summary: Check whether a contact may be reached
post.description: Called only by the services that contact people, with the shared secret and no user token; the Organization is named in the body. Always answers 200 with a result: allowed (with the basis) or denied (with a code and, for a suppressed address, the Suppression reason). Fails closed: a missing or deleted Organization and an unknown Prospect are `consent.missing`. Every answer about a live Organization is written to the audit log first; if that fails the call fails with 500 and the caller must treat it as `consent.unavailable` and not contact. An Agent may call, text or message on WhatsApp only with a granted Contact Consent for the channel; email needs no consent, only that the address is not suppressed; LinkedIn is not allowed to an Agent. A suppressed address is refused for every purpose. A check by address reads no consent, so a channel that needs consent is `consent.missing`. A Prospect together with the address about to be used (`phone`, `email` or `linkedinUrl`, by the channel) must name one of that Prospect's own addresses, or the answer is `consent.missing`; Suppression is then tested on that address and consent is read from the Prospect's ledger.
